key_gap: vs baseline: the human opens with the horizon split and the irreversibility floor as first-class moves ('a stock that never comes back', 'three dates are three different cities') and never re-derives them; the v5 AI reached the same decision (A, +20.1B) and numbers but burned a WHY-stage hypothesis re-deriving that the rate war cannot happen (Efficiency 3 vs 5) and produced the irreversibility rule more mechanically (Insight 3 vs 4). The routed v6 run closes all three gaps: the m062 contract makes the 2030/2050/2100 split + dual-rate schedule (3% ordinary / 1.5% irreversibility floor) + breakeven sensitivity the first-class opening, the m050 safety-inversion pass prices the barrier's own failure modes (breach crest, deferred $900M reinforcement, financing spread, wetland valuation), the m007 ruin screen frames C as the ruin path and overdesign as cheap tail insurance, and the insight pass reproduces the human's signature reframe (I1: three different cities; I2: the rate debate is arithmetic theater).
learning_signal: On intergenerational infrastructure decisions with an irreversible resource, the horizon split and the irreversibility rate floor must be the FIRST moves of the analysis — installed as a module contract, not re-derived: discount ordinary flows at the social rate and irreversible stocks on a declining-rate floor with the reason stated, evaluate the policy at 2030/2050/2100 with explicit cash flows, and demonstrate the breakeven rate across the defensible range so the discount-rate debate cannot stall the decision (the v5 efficiency gap was exactly the wasted re-derivation the contract removes). Pair the recommendation with the mandatory ruin screen (m007: outcome distribution, one-shot check, floor/Kelly, probability provenance, decline/restructure alternative) and the safety-inversion enumeration of the chosen plan's own failure modes (m050) — the routed gate structure converts the human's intuition into mandatory outputs.
suggested_improvement: Keep the m062 contract as the standing first-class pass on climate/infrastructure cases with irreversibility (horizon split -> dual-rate schedule -> breakeven -> tail mitigation), triggered by the finance/strategy + guarantee signature; the m003/m007 gates deliver the ruin and inversion coverage the human gets by intuition, so the rate question is closed by computation before any stage can enter it; retain the insight pass (S2) as the packet gate — it is what supplies the 'three different cities' reframe the human produces by narrative.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure style failed by design — sign-invariant NPVs (+960M/+835M/+694M/+488M) computed then ignored, the unresolved 1.4%-vs-5.5% rate declared a binding gate, and the 1-in-1000 hospital-overwhelm tail declared decisive ('false security is worse than vulnerability'), producing a defer-and-monitor verdict. The v5 AI already won on the horizon-disjointness check; the routed v6 run hardens the win structurally: m001 rebuilt the decision from fundamentals (dominance, complementarity/real-option, flow-completion by ~2045, this-cycle-only budget), m018 steelmanned the 'false security' objection in its strongest form and answered it (messaging vs measured value; the measure as pre-commitment to the barrier), m019 priced the half-benefit and moral-hazard exposures, and the m003 inversion gate ranked 'long-horizon question gates near-term decision' as the #1 failure category — the two registered trap arguments are destroyed by horizon placement, not by authority.
learning_signal: When a brief mixes long-horizon noise with a short-horizon decision at the same resolution, the horizon-disjointness check must run BEFORE any rate choice: identify which horizon contains the decision-relevant flows, compute NPV sign-invariance across the full defensible range, declare the disputed horizon out-of-scope with a scheduled review trigger in the packet, and steelman the strongest objection (here 'false security') in its strongest form — it is a messaging argument, answered by complementarity + pre-commitment, never a reason to withhold a sign-invariant complementary measure. The registered trap is the signature move applied to the wrong horizon: horizon separation is mandatory, but which horizon holds the decision's flows is the actual gate.
suggested_improvement: Install horizon-disjointness as a mandatory gate (m001/m018/m003 combination) on any decision whose brief supplies adjacent long-horizon noise, and require the out-of-scope log + review trigger in every packet; keep the m019 red-team half-benefit pricing as the standard exposure check on benefit-led measures; on fully specified recommendation tasks with no deadline flag, use the closed-scope fast path (P8) so the verdict commits at DO without re-derivation — the v5 run tied efficiency at 4.0, the v6 run takes it at 4.5.
